title: uncanny
skill: Choose the more natural use of uncanny and explain why: (a) The twins, who had never met, used exactly the same unusual expressions. (b) The bus arrived at its advertised time.

title: commemoration
skill: An invitation reads: “Come to our commemoration—a loud costume contest with prizes!” What expectation does commemoration create, and which word better fits the advertised event?

title: factor in
skill: The walk starts at 7:30. Getting there takes 15 minutes and entry takes another 10. What is the latest departure time? Explain your calculation in one sentence using factor in.

title: iron out
skill: Replace the vague reply “We’ll deal with it” with a specific two-sentence update using iron out. The problem: two volunteers have been assigned the same shift and the closing shift is empty.

title: the devil is in the details
skill: Which overlooked detail best justifies this idiom? A: The poster is orange. B: Registration closes six hours before the contest. C: The event has a cheerful name. Give one practical consequence.

title: a double-edged sword
skill: Complete this balanced assessment with one benefit and one drawback: “A public event hashtag is a double-edged sword: ___, yet ___.” Keep both points connected to public visibility.

title: I see your point, although I would qualify it slightly.
skill: A colleague claims, “Every part of the event must be scary.” Respond with the target phrase, preserve the useful part of the idea, and add one clear limitation.

title:
Double, double toil and trouble;
Fire burn, and cauldron bubble.
skill: You are directing this line for a school performance. Identify one repetition and one repeated consonant sound. Explain how you would use them in delivery.

title: Inversion after only then
skill: Rewrite as one sentence beginning Only then: “We tested the costume in the dark. At that moment, we noticed that the sleeves covered the reflective strips.”

title: What would you like to do for Halloween?
skill: Your neighbor replies, “I don’t celebrate Halloween, actually.” Write a friendly response that acknowledges this and smoothly opens a different topic.

title: A little room to choose
skill: Outline four paragraphs improving a school fair. Include two different changes, a concrete example for each, and a conclusion linking their benefits.
